text: fit_logistic_fe() replaces logis_fe(): binary binomial outcomes, SerBIN BAN. test() replaces test_fe(): statistic (exact, score, Wald) x variance (naive, robust, stabilized) one fixed set output columns; naive Wald statistic uses case-mix variance (gamma_variance()), depend covariate origin; restricted score test 1.0.3 back score_type = "restricted". summary() replaces summary_fe_covar(); likelihood-ratio refit respects fit’s bound. confint() gives intervals provider effects; standardize() replaces SR_output() maps limits ratios rates; direct_expectation() replaces direct_exp(). test_measure() replaces test_SM() adds log scale.

what: Linear, random-effect and correlated random-effect models (rewritten from 1.0.3)
title: pprof 2.0.1
text: pp_data() detects takes outcome type (binary, binomial, continuous); sim_kecc() simulates continuous outcomes. fit_linear_fe() replaces linear_fe(): within-provider regression instead dense block-diagonal centring matrix; gamma_variance() offers case-mix variance (1.0.3’s “simplified”, exactly sigma^2 / n_i) “full” one; provider covariate tests use t distribution n - m - p degrees freedom every model-based statistic (1.0.3 mixed normal t references); patient-clustered robust variance new. fit_logistic_fe(penalty = "firth") replaces logis_firth() extends binomial trials; object logistic_fe fit, every test standardization applies. kernel follows ParaFLR (UM-KevinHe/hpc-flr): per-provider work independent threads, p x p reductions whole-data matrix products result depend thread count. test(statistic = "lr") adds ParaFLR’s likelihood-ratio test one provider effect parameters fixed (penalized likelihood Firth fit). fit_logistic_re(), fit_logistic_cre(), fit_linear_re(), fit_linear_cre() replace logis_re(), logis_cre(), linear_re(), linear_cre() (lme4 wrappers): random effects coefficients$alpha, conditional variances post_var; CRE decomposition names columns <x>_within <x>_between defaults every covariate; tests fixed effects use 2 * pnorm(-|z|) (1.0.3 computed 2 * (1 - pnorm(z)), wrong negative statistics); standardization offers observed (default) predicted numerator. direct standardized difference linear models relative population (row-weighted mean effects), direct ratio logistic models always ; 1.0.3 used median linear model .
